Supple

SUP-ul · adjective

Hear It

No recording available for this word.

What It Means

Supple is bending and moving easily and gracefully; flexible.

The gymnast's supple limbs folded into the pretzel-like pose without a single strained muscle.

Worked Example

After months of stretching, his once-stiff hamstrings became supple enough to touch his toes flat-palmed.

Supple can describe a flexible body, but also flexible materials -- supple leather, for example, bends easily instead of cracking.

How Supple Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

flexible

flexible: able to bend easily without breaking

lithe

lithe: thin, supple, and graceful in movement

Antonyms

rigid

rigid: unable to bend; stiff

stiff

stiff: not easily bent; inflexible

How Strong Is It? — pliable → lissome → supple

pliable vs. supple

pliable vs. supple: Pliable describes a more basic kind of easy bending or shaping, without supple's added sense of gracefulness.

lissome vs. supple

lissome vs. supple: Lissome adds an even more graceful, almost effortless flexibility, often describing a dancer's whole body.

The pieces

prefix — sub-

prefix — sub-: under (Latin)

root — plicare

root — plicare: to fold (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Supple comes from Latin supplex (originally 'kneeling, bending under'), built from sub- ('under') plus plicare ('to fold') -- describing something that bends or folds easily, whether a body or a material.
